tier_reason: Upgraded C->B: the numbers come from the peer-reviewed SIGMOD 2024 paper (arXiv:2308.13632), whose Section 5.4.3 swaps RocksDB's built-in Bloom filter for ChainedFilter at equal filter space and reports P99 point-query latency falling from about 31us to under 20us (36% lower). It is not A because the RocksDB integration and benchmark code is not in the repo. The repo has only src/Algorithm1-2, Static Dictionary, Random Access Huffman Coding and Self-Adaptive Hashing, and none of them runs a Bloom baseline, although the CPU (i9-10980XE) and compiler (g++ 7.5.0 -O3) are stated.

corrections.claimed_speedup: SIGMOD 2024 paper: up to 36% lower P99 tail point-query latency than RocksDB's built-in Bloom filter at the same filter space (|U|=16M existing-item queries: about 31us for Bloom vs under 20us for ChainedFilter); up to 31% fewer external memory accesses than raw Cuckoo Hashing; 26% extra space over the theoretical lower bound for an implicit static dictionary; 0.22 extra bits/item over the lower bound for lossless compression; up to 99.1% less filter space than the original Learned Bloom Filter
corrections.workload: RocksDB (all SSTables in L0, default 64MB write buffer, 36-byte random keys and 64-byte values, 4M-16M items) P70/P99 point-query latency with ChainedFilter replacing the built-in Bloom filter, versus Bloom-only filters at 0x/1x/2x space; also external-memory accesses for Cuckoo Hashing, static-dictionary space and Learned Bloom Filter space
corrections.hardware: Intel Core i9-10980XE @ 3.00GHz (the paper says '36 Intel Core i9-10980XE CPU'), 24.8MiB L3, 128GB DRAM
corrections.compiler_and_flags: g++ 7.5.0 (Ubuntu 7.5.0-6ubuntu2), -O3; the README says C++17, but the Self-Adaptive Hashing Makefile uses --std=c++11 -O3 -g
corrections.caveats: No LICENSE file, so all rights are reserved by default and the code is reference/study-only. The repo says the code is there to help readers understand the paper's algorithms; it is not a packaged library. The headline RocksDB P99 experiment (paper Section 5.4) has no code in the repo, which only covers Algorithms 1-2, the static dictionary, random-access Huffman and self-adaptive Cuckoo hashing. The 36% gain is for existing-key queries at |U|=16M; for non-existing keys at 16M, ChainedFilter latency rises depending on which SSTable reports the false positive. Last commit was 2023-04-27, more than 3 years ago.

notes: The numbers match the README and the arXiv abstract; the paper was accepted at SIGMOD 2024 (arXiv comment and PDF header). The tier goes up to B because of the peer-reviewed paper, so the verdict is confirm. maintenance_status changes from stale to abandoned, since the last commit was 3.4 years ago.

tier_reason: These are first-party numbers from a single run in the README. The benchmark code is public (src/bin/benchmark.rs) and the release profile is in Cargo.toml, but no CPU model is given and the Rust toolchain version is not pinned ('stable'). The Bloom and Cuckoo(2,4) baselines are the author's own from-scratch implementations, not incumbent libraries.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Windowed cuckoo (2,2): 1.5958 bytes/item vs Bloom's 1.8034 (README: about 12% less memory) and Cuckoo(2,4)'s 2.1299 (about 25% less) at similar FPR (2^-10 target); lookup 60.28 ns vs Bloom's 81.59 ns and Cuckoo's 61.19 ns (essentially tied with cuckoo). Inserts are slower: 162.97 ns vs 58.74 ns for Cuckoo(2,4) and 93.61 ns for Bloom, and max load is 0.9575 vs 0.9780 for Cuckoo
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Rust stable toolchain (version not pinned, rust-toolchain.toml), edition 2024, release profile lto=thin, codegen-units=1
corrections.caveats: Third-party Rust reimplementation of arXiv:2505.05847 (Smaller and More Flexible Cuckoo Filters), not the paper authors' code. The baselines are the author's own Bloom and Cuckoo(2,4) implementations, not established libraries. The README table is one run (defaults: 100k items, 200k queries, k=10), with no CPU model and no pinned toolchain version. Inserts are about 2.8x slower than the conventional cuckoo filter. It uses a non-cryptographic hash that is not safe against adversarial input. 0 stars; created and pushed around 2026-09-03.

notes: The README numbers match the record exactly, and the 12%/25% memory figures are stated on the page. Metadata checks out: MIT license, not a fork, 0 stars, last commit 2026-09-03, active. The claim now includes the insert-speed regression the record left out.
